business_problem: The Egyptian Tax Authority needed to digitize invoice and receipt collection so it could reduce shadow-economy leakage, improve compliance, and replace paper-heavy tax reporting with a more transparent data foundation.
solution_summary: The Ministry of Finance and Egyptian Tax Authority built new e-invoicing and e-receipt capabilities on Microsoft platforms to capture transaction data digitally rather than depending on paper forms and taxpayer self-reporting alone. The architecture is meant to improve the state's view of economic activity, reduce arbitrary estimations in tax examinations, and create an electronic database that can support deeper supply-chain visibility and future AI-assisted audits. Key components include Microsoft SQL Server stores the e-invoicing and e-receipt data that forms the core electronic tax database; Windows Server supports the platform services that run the digital invoicing environment; Power BI surfaces reporting and analysis over the digital tax data foundation. The new systems are easier for taxpayers to use, have improved the trend in compliance, and have reduced tax examination effort to several hours while giving ETA a foundation for broader digital transformation.
